title: Source-first monetary inventory: Monster Manual and Monster Manual II

scope.purpose: Candidate inventory of monetary prices, fees, costs, and explicit valuations found during full-page PDF text-layer census followed by visual inspection of selected original pages.
scope.coverageClaim: This is not a claim that every price in either book has been found. Search cues are fallible; unflagged/image-only or OCR-corrupted pages may contain monetary claims. Every page remains represented in the census, and unreviewed candidates stay explicit.
scope.sourcePriority: Original private PDF scan is authoritative. Text-layer/OCR cues locate candidates and do not establish source wording or absence.
scope.privacy: Original PDFs and rendered source pages remain private and are not included in the repository artifact.

screeningMethod.tool: PyMuPDF text extraction from every page of both hash-verified PDFs; page text char count recorded.
screeningMethod.candidateRule: Any page with one or more configured currency, transaction, valuation, or gem cues is a broad text candidate. This deliberately overincludes treasure tables, XP labels, carrying-weight values, and OCR noise.
limitations: Text-layer page census is not visual proof of all page content.
Image-only pages and OCR-corrupted/missed wording may contain unflagged prices.
Unreviewed cue pages are pending visual review; they are not marked as having no price.
The page-cue screen is not exhaustive and does not establish whole-book completeness.

claims.amountOrFormula: (100–600 gp per elephant tusk) × 1.5 = 150–900 gp per mammoth tusk (derived)
claims.conditions: Mammoth tusks are 50% heavier and their value is proportionately higher. Apply the explicit proportional value relation to the Elephant value of 100–600 gp each. The resulting 150–900 gp per mammoth tusk is derived, not a printed range.
notes: The 1.5 factor follows the explicit proportional value relation; physical weight alone is not a monetary amount.
Derived per-tusk valuation only. No pair, herd, market adjustment or tusk-condition price is inferred.

unresolvedCandidates.sourceReading: Text layer claims a 5,000 gp market value per egg.
unresolvedCandidates.disposition: Do not treat as verified monetary claim; the corresponding wording/value was not visible on the inspected source page. Preserve as OCR/text-layer mismatch for follow-up.

unresolvedCandidates.sourceReading: Nuggets are described as “the size of 5 gold pieces.”
unresolvedCandidates.disposition: Do not interpret “5 gold pieces” as monetary value; source wording may describe physical size/weight.

unresolvedCandidates.sourceReading: Source mentions 5–30 pieces of jewelry of low base worth and an average weight of 150 gp each.
unresolvedCandidates.disposition: Do not treat 150 gp as a monetary value; the source explicitly labels it average weight. The low-base-worth wording gives no numeric price.

unresolvedCandidates.sourceReading: These are “a hundred times” the average 50 gp feather value.
unresolvedCandidates.disposition: Retained as relative formula; do not infer a separate 5,000 gp price for each part because the unit scope is not explicit.

exclusions.reason: “10,000 gold pieces” is explicitly weight/carrying capacity, not price or value.
“2,500 GP wt.” is a weight limit, not a monetary amount.
Gold-piece units describe carried weight/load, not prices.
Treasure-category codes/probability tables and coin quantities are not prices; page reviewed visually.
Randomly generated 3–18 platinum pieces and 5–20 gems have no stated monetary valuation; not price claims.
Random treasure quantities (10–40 gp, 5–20 pp) are treasure-generation results, not prices or valuations.
Negative sale statement: the source says shadow dragons cannot be subdued and sold; no price is stated.
Trade or purchase is mentioned without an amount or specific monetary value.
No monetary amount or value stated in visually inspected passage.
Generic “items of value” with no monetary amount.
Random coin counts/odds and probabilities are excluded as treasure-generation quantities; listed gem and item value thresholds are recorded as separate claims.
Coin-type/count probabilities are treasure-generation quantities, not monetary price claims; gem base value and magic-item ceiling are recorded separately.

coverageSummary.interpretation: Counts describe this bounded audit and its documented records only; they do not estimate all-book completeness or error rates.

visualReviewMethod.rendering: Full-page raster views rendered locally from the hash-verified private PDFs with PyMuPDF at approximately 1.3–1.4 scale; one Pech passage was additionally inspected in a 3x local detail render.
visualReviewMethod.bounds: OCR text-block bounding boxes in PDF-page points, top-left origin. These bounds are provisional and are not pixel-calibrated; visual confirmation of a value does not upgrade its coordinate bounds.
visualReviewMethod.privateArtifacts: Source PDFs and rendered images remain outside the repository.
